newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa industrials firm, golds dip.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa industrials firm, golds dip.

text.p: South African shares swiftly overcame early nervousness on Wednesday to race ahead and post solid gains in heavy trade as positive sentiment continued to sweep through the market, dealers said.
A renewed fall in the bullion price to below $343 -- just a day after a mini-rally sparked hopes of an upturn -- gave dealers a fright early on and most shares opened down.

But as the rand roared ahead to break through the psychologically important 4.50 level against the U.S. dollar, South African shares quickly won back all their losses and headed firmly for positive territory.
The all-share index added 38.1 points to 6,804.1 as the industrials index adds 25.2 points to 8,133.4.
Volumes were a huge 996 million rands worth of shares. The causes of the positive sentiment gripping the market lie in the strong rand, healthy bond market and bullish hopes for an interest rate cut.
Speculation that President Nelson Mandela may soon make a major announcement on removing foreign exchange controls has also served to stoke the fires of the bullish market.
Gold shares had a difficult day in the wake of bullion's renewed drop and the index lost 14.6 points to 1,373.7.
But dealers said that the performance of the index had been better than had been hoped for and only about a third of Tuesday's heady gains had been wiped out.
